body:
PR #2005 for TASK-1290 — the gate that would have caught tonight's largest failure class, and its own lane avoided that class

Open on task-1290, +841, BLOCKED on normal review gating. Spec set to Done per the lane-lifecycle fix, so a merge auto-bumps it without you. No verdict from me; I wrote the prompt.

WHAT IT DOES. Wires the existing `aida criteria` tracer into three points: `queue done` (warn by default, refuse under `[protocol] enforce = "refuse"`, `--force` overrides with a ledgered comment), the `gh pr create` choke point shared by ship/zen/pr ship (warn only), and round 1 of the headless reviewer prompt, which now carries the untraced list so the reviewer CITES it rather than discovering it.

I VERIFIED THE TWO THINGS THAT MATTER.

Reuse, not reimplementation — the acceptance criterion you would have checked. Everything sits on `crate::criteria::build_criteria_report`, the function backing `aida criteria`. The new module adds only pure policy and formatting on top. No second tracer.

Quiet when clean, tested. `queue_done_is_quiet_when_all_criteria_are_traced` constructs a genuinely traced criterion and asserts silence. That was the binding constraint — a gate that speaks on every run is one people learn to ignore, which is how the hub-drift warnings became background noise for 32 hours.

And all five acceptance criteria have a named test driving the REAL BINARY through CLI dispatch, not the helper functions. That is worth calling out because it is the exact class this spec exists to catch: "the acceptance named a boundary and the implementation tested below it", at least seven prior instances, and BUG-1291's round-1 finding tonight made it eight. The lane implementing the detector did not commit the defect the detector detects.

WHERE TASK-1277 PLUGS IN, since the spec told it to extend a gate that does not exist yet. All policy is behind one `criteria_gate::evaluate(report, enforce_mode)` called from a single choke point next to the existing review-verdict gate, and `read_enforce_mode` reads only the `[protocol].enforce` key it needs — so TASK-1277 can add its own protocol-item keys under the same section and fold its Warn/Refuse lines in without a refactor. Documented in the module doc rather than left as tribal knowledge. That was the risk I flagged when dispatching it, and it came back addressed rather than ignored.

Reported, not re-run by me: 5130 tests pass, fmt clean.

The pre-commit provenance gate caught `///` doc comments ending with trace markers again — six of eleven lanes now. It is the highest-yield gate we have and none of those would have been caught by review.

WORTH CONNECTING TO TASK-1289. I sent you a separate note arguing that spec should be split rather than re-driven a fifth time. If TASK-1290 merges, the reviewer prompt starts carrying the untraced-criteria list into round 1 — which is precisely the information TASK-1289's rounds have been rediscovering from scratch each time. Sequencing TASK-1290 ahead of any further TASK-1289 attempt may be worth more than the split itself.
